title: Linear algebra with NumPy
intro: A linear system, eigenvalues, a least-squares fit and the singular values, in Python with NumPy, in the reader's browser.

nodes.title: A symmetric matrix
nodes.code:
import numpy as np
A = np.array([[2.0, 1.0], [1.0, 3.0]])
b = np.array([1.0, 2.0])

nodes.title: Solve $Ax = b$
nodes.code:
x = np.linalg.solve(A, b)
print(x)
print(np.allclose(A @ x, b))

nodes.title: Its eigenvalues
nodes.code:
w, V = np.linalg.eigh(A)
print(np.round(w, 6))
print(np.allclose(A @ V, V * w))

nodes.title: A least-squares line
nodes.code:
M = np.column_stack([np.ones(4), np.arange(1, 5)])
ys = np.array([2.1, 3.9, 6.2, 7.8])
coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(M, ys, rcond=None)
print("intercept %.3f, slope %.3f" % tuple(coef))
